request: Create a lesson designing a fair comparison of two maze solvers from the logs and resources. Require executable allocation or pairing, a blank operations table and limits on any performance claim.
objective: Separate solver and map-difficulty differences and distinguish independent maps from repeat deterministic runs.

sources.text: Fictional coding-club log: solver A used a median of120 operations on easy maps; solver B used80 on medium maps. The old maps, map counts and individual logs were not retained.

Twenty new fixed maze files are available, ten labeled easy and ten medium. Both solvers can run on every file. Files are immutable; use the same machine, compiler options and fixed solver seeds. A solver can be run on a file without altering it.

Count calls to the supplied step function until the target is reached; save map ID, difficulty, solver, seed, run order, operation count and success/failure status. Stop at10000 operations and mark unreached targets as censored failures, not solved in zero operations. No new runs have occurred.
